source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 12.

sections.heading: 1. The Sky and Celestial Bodies
points: Objects in the sky = **celestial bodies**: the **Sun, stars, planets, moons, asteroids, comets, meteors**.
**Stars** are huge, hot bodies that give out their **own light** (the **Sun is our nearest star**).
**Planets** do **not** give their own light — they **shine by reflecting** the Sun's light.
**Constellations** = groups of stars forming recognisable patterns (e.g. **Ursa Major / Saptarshi (Big Dipper)**, **Orion**).

sections.heading: 2. The Solar System
points: The **Solar System** = the **Sun** and everything that orbits it.
**Eight planets**, in order from the Sun: **Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune** ("My Very Efficient Mother Just Served Us Noodles").
**Inner (rocky) planets:** Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.
**Outer (gas giant) planets:** Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
**Mercury** = nearest to the Sun & smallest; **Jupiter** = largest planet; **Venus** = brightest & hottest; **Saturn** = famous rings.
Between Mars and Jupiter lies the **asteroid belt**.

sections.heading: 3. The Earth and the Moon
points: **Earth** = the only planet known to support **life** (right temperature, water, oxygen); the **"Blue Planet."**
**Rotation** (spinning on its axis, ~24 hours) causes **day and night**; **revolution** around the Sun (~365¼ days) with the tilted axis causes **seasons**.
The **Moon** = Earth's natural **satellite**; has no light of its own (reflects sunlight); its changing shapes are the **phases of the Moon**.
The Moon has no air/water; footprints stay because there is no wind.

sections.heading: 4. Other Bodies and Space Exploration
points: **Asteroids** = small rocky bodies (mainly in the asteroid belt).
**Comets** = icy bodies with a glowing **tail** when near the Sun.
**Meteors ('shooting stars')** = bits of rock burning up in the atmosphere; if one lands, it is a **meteorite**.
A **galaxy** = a huge system of stars, gas and dust; our galaxy is the **Milky Way (Akash Ganga)**.
**ISRO** is India's space agency — missions like **Chandrayaan** (Moon) and **Mangalyaan** (Mars).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Stars give own light; planets shine by reflecting sunlight; Sun = nearest star.
8 planets (Sun outward): Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Inner rocky: Mercury–Mars; outer gas giants: Jupiter–Neptune; asteroid belt between Mars & Jupiter.
Jupiter = largest; Mercury = smallest & nearest; Venus = brightest/hottest; Saturn = rings.
Rotation → day & night; revolution + tilt → seasons; Moon = Earth's satellite (phases).
Our galaxy = Milky Way (Akash Ganga); India's space agency = ISRO.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Planets do NOT produce light** — they reflect the Sun's light; only **stars** shine on their own.
**Jupiter** is the largest planet; **Mercury** is the smallest and closest to the Sun.
**Venus** (not Mercury) is the hottest planet, due to its thick atmosphere.
The **asteroid belt** lies **between Mars and Jupiter**.
Day and night are due to **rotation**; seasons are due to **revolution + axial tilt** — don't swap.
